description: Pineapple Buns, or Bo Lo Bao, are a beloved Hong Kong bakery classic, known for their soft, fluffy bread and distinctive crispy, sweet, crumbly topping. Despite the name, there's no pineapple in them; the topping simply resembles a pineapple's textured skin. These golden-brown delights are perfect for breakfast, a snack, or alongside a cup of milk tea.

instructions.title: Prepare the Bun Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine bread flour, 40g granulated sugar, milk powder, instant dry yeast, and salt. Mix well. Add the beaten egg and warm milk. Mix with a spatula until a shaggy dough forms. Turn out onto a clean surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth. Incorporate the 30g softened unsalted butter and knead for another 5-7 minutes until the dough is elastic and passes the windowpane test. Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Make the Pineapple Topping
instructions.text: While the dough is proofing, prepare the topping. In a medium bowl, cream together 60g softened unsalted butter and 60g powdered sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolk and vanilla extract (if using) until well combined. Sift in the all-purpose flour and baking powder. Mix until a soft, crumbly dough forms. Do not overmix. Cover the topping dough and refrigerate until ready to use.

instructions.title: Divide and Shape the Dough
instructions.text: Once the bun dough has doubled, gently punch it down and divide it into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a smooth ball. Place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between each bun. Lightly cover and let rest for 10 minutes.

instructions.title: Apply the Topping
instructions.text: Take the pineapple topping out of the refrigerator. Divide it into 8 equal portions. Flatten each portion between two pieces of parchment paper or plastic wrap into a round disc, roughly 4-5 inches in diameter. Carefully peel off one side of the wrap and invert the topping disc onto a bun. Gently press to adhere, shaping it over the top of the bun, leaving the bottom edge exposed. Repeat for all buns.

instructions.title: Second Proof and Preheat Oven
instructions.text: Once all buns are topped, cover them loosely with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let them rise in a warm place for another 30-40 minutes, or until visibly puffy. Towards the end of the second proofing, preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Prepare the egg wash by whisking together 1 egg yolk and 1 tsp water.

instructions.title: Bake the Pineapple Buns
instructions.text: Brush the tops of the pineapple topping generously with the egg wash. Be careful not to let the egg wash drip down the sides onto the exposed bun dough, as this can hinder its rise. Bake in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and crispy, and the buns are cooked through. Let cool slightly on a wire rack before serving.

tips: For an extra crispy topping, refrigerate the topping dough for at least 30 minutes before shaping. This makes it easier to handle and prevents it from melting too quickly in the oven.

If you dont have milk powder, you can omit it, but it adds a nice depth of flavor and softness to the bun dough. Alternatively, use a splash less warm milk and enrich the liquid with a bit of evaporated milk.

Pineapple Buns are best enjoyed fresh and warm. If storing, keep them in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a toaster oven for a few minutes to restore crispness.
article:
Craving that iconic sweet and crumbly topping paired with a soft, fluffy bun? You're not alone! The Pineapple Bun, or Bo Lo Bao (菠蘿包), is a beloved staple in Chinese bakeries and Hong Kong-style cafes worldwide. Its distinctive appearance, reminiscent of a pineapple's skin, and its delightful contrast of textures make it an irresistible treat. While its name might suggest a fruity filling, the magic lies entirely in its crispy, sugary crust. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that magic at home, this comprehensive Pineapple Bun Recipe is for you. Get ready to embark on a delicious baking adventure that will fill your kitchen with the aroma of freshly baked Chinese pastries.

## What is Pineapple Bun Bo Lo Bao?

The Pineapple Bun, or Bo Lo Bao, is a quintessential Hong Kong-style sweet bun, famous for its unique crunchy, sugary crust that tops a soft, fluffy bread base. Despite its name, there is no pineapple fruit in the bun itself. The "pineapple" refers solely to the distinct cracked, golden-brown pattern on the topping, which resembles the skin of the tropical fruit. This clever nomenclature is a testament to its visual appeal. Originating in Hong Kong during the 1940s, these buns quickly became a popular fixture in cha chaan tengs (Hong Kong-style diners) and bakeries, often enjoyed for breakfast or afternoon tea. Many home bakers search for an authentic Pineapple Bun Recipe to capture that nostalgic taste and texture. The allure of the Bo Lo Bao lies in the delightful textural interplay: the melt-in-your-mouth sweetness of the crunchy topping giving way to the tender, slightly sweet bread underneath. It’s a simple yet profoundly satisfying pastry that has captured hearts globally.

## Ingredients You Need

Gathering the right ingredients is the first step towards a successful Pineapple Bun Recipe. Quality ingredients make a noticeable difference in the final taste and texture.

**For the Bread Dough:**
*   3 cups (360g) bread flour (or all-purpose flour for a softer crumb)
*   1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar
*   1 teaspoon instant dry yeast
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 large egg, lightly beaten
*   3/4 cup (180ml) warm milk (around 100-110°F / 38-43°C)
*   2 tablespoons (28g) unsalted butter, softened

**For the Pineapple Topping:**
*   1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter, softened
*   1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar
*   1 large egg yolk
*   1 1/2 cups (180g) all-purpose flour
*   1 tablespoon milk powder (optional, for richer flavor)
*   1/2 teaspoon baking powder (optional, for a crispier topping)
*   1-2 tablespoons milk (if needed, to adjust consistency)

**For Egg Wash (for topping):**
*   1 egg yolk, mixed with 1 tablespoon water

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Following this Pineapple Bun Recipe step-by-step will ensure delicious results that rival your favorite bakery.

**1. Prepare the Bread Dough:**
    *   In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Whisk briefly to combine.
    *   Add the beaten egg and warm milk to the dry ingredients. Mix with a spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
    *   Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for about 10 minutes, or until smooth and elastic. If using a stand mixer with a dough hook, knead on medium speed for 7-8 minutes.
    *   Add the softened butter and continue kneading for another 5-7 minutes until the butter is fully incorporated and the dough is very smooth, elastic, and passes the windowpane test (you can stretch a small piece of dough thin enough to see light through it without tearing).
    *   Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it proof in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

**2. Prepare the Pineapple Topping:**
    *   While the dough is proofing, make the topping. In a medium bowl, cream together the softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
    *   Beat in the egg yolk until fully incorporated.
    *   Add the flour, milk powder (if using), and baking powder (if using) to the butter mixture. Mix until a crumbly dough forms. If the mixture is too dry, add milk one teaspoon at a time until it comes together. Avoid overmixing.
    *   Shape the topping dough into a log, wrap it in plastic wrap, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. This makes it easier to handle.

**3. Assemble the Buns:**
    *   Once the bread dough has doubled, gently punch it down to release the air.
    *   Divide the dough into 10-12 equal pieces (about 60-70g each). Roll each piece into a smooth ball. Place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between each.
    *   Take the chilled topping dough and divide it into the same number of pieces as your bread dough.
    *   On a lightly floured surface or between two pieces of plastic wrap, flatten each piece of topping dough into a disc about 3-4 inches (7-10 cm) in diameter, large enough to cover the top of a dough ball.
    *   Carefully place a topping disc over each bread dough ball, gently pressing down and molding it to cover the top and sides of the bun. The topping should cover about 2/3 of the bun.
    *   Using the back of a knife or a dough scraper, gently score a crosshatch pattern onto the topping of each bun. Be careful not to cut too deep into the bread dough.

**4. Second Proof and Bake:**
    *   Cover the assembled buns loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let them proof in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
    *   Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
    *   Just before baking, brush the scored topping of each bun with the egg yolk wash.
    *   Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and cracked, and the buns are cooked through.
    *   Remove from the oven and let cool slightly on a wire rack before serving.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Mastering this Pineapple Bun Recipe takes a little practice, but these tips will help you achieve bakery-quality buns every time:

*   **Kneading is Key:** Don't skimp on kneading the bread dough. Proper gluten development is essential for a soft, fluffy crumb. A smooth, elastic dough that passes the windowpane test is your goal.
*   **Warm Milk, Not Hot:** When proofing yeast, ensure your milk is warm (like bathwater, around 100-110°F / 38-43°C). Too hot will kill the yeast, too cold will slow it down.
*   **Don't Over-Proof:** While adequate proofing is important, over-proofing can lead to a yeasty flavor and a collapsed bun. The dough should double in size, but not look overly airy or bubbly.
*   **Chilled Topping:** Chilling the topping dough is crucial. It makes it less sticky and easier to handle, preventing it from melting too quickly when placed on the warm bread dough.
*   **Gentle Scoring:** Score the topping with a light but firm hand. You want to create the distinctive pineapple pattern without cutting too deeply into the bread dough itself, which could hinder its rise.
*   **Even Baking:** If your oven has hot spots, rotate the baking sheet halfway through baking to ensure even browning.
*   **Optional Custard Powder:** For an even richer flavor and a more vibrant yellow color in the topping, you can substitute 1-2 tablespoons of flour with custard powder in the topping mixture.

## Serving Suggestions

Pineapple Buns are best enjoyed warm, fresh from the oven, when the topping is at its crispiest and the bread is at its softest.

*   **The Classic Way:** In Hong Kong, it's common to slice a warm Pineapple Bun horizontally and insert a thick slice of cold butter (known as Bo Lo Yau). The butter melts into the warm bun, creating an incredible salty-sweet, rich experience.
*   **With a Drink:** Pair your bun with a cup of hot Hong Kong-style milk tea, coffee, or even just a glass of cold milk for a comforting breakfast or afternoon snack.
*   **Plain and Simple:** Sometimes, the bun is perfect all on its own, allowing the textures and subtle sweetness to shine through.
*   **As a Dessert:** While traditionally a snack, a Pineapple Bun can also serve as a delightful, light dessert.

## Variations and Substitutions

While this Pineapple Bun Recipe focuses on the classic, don't hesitate to experiment with variations to suit your taste or dietary needs.

*   **Filled Pineapple Buns:** Many bakeries offer Pineapple Buns with various fillings.
    *   **Custard:** A smooth, sweet egg custard filling is a popular choice.
    *   **Red Bean Paste:** Sweetened red bean paste adds a traditional Asian flavor.
    *   **Char Siu:** For a savory twist, some versions include diced char siu (Chinese BBQ pork) in a savory sauce.
*   **Topping Enhancements:**
    *   **Coconut Flakes:** Add a tablespoon or two of desiccated coconut to the topping mixture for a tropical aroma and chew.
    *   **Sesame Seeds:** Sprinkle some white sesame seeds on the topping before baking for added texture and nutty flavor.
*   **Flour Choices:**
    *   **Bread Flour:** Using 100% bread flour will give you a chewier, more structured bun.
    *   **All-Purpose Flour:** Using all-purpose flour will result in a softer, more cake-like crumb. A mix of both can offer a good balance.
*   **Dairy-Free Options:**
    *   Substitute regular milk with plant-based milk (almond, soy, oat).
    *   Use a high-quality plant-based butter alternative for both the dough and the topping.
    *   For the egg wash, you can use a plant-based milk or a mixture of plant-based milk and a pinch of turmeric for color.
*   **Sugar Adjustments:** You can slightly adjust the sugar content in both the dough and the topping according to your preference for sweetness.

Making Pineapple Buns at home is a rewarding experience that brings a piece of Chinese bakery culture directly to your kitchen. With this detailed Pineapple Bun Recipe, you're well on your way to baking these iconic, delicious treats that are sure to impress family and friends. Enjoy the process, and savor every bite of your homemade Bo Lo Bao!
